source.work: tRPC documentation, authorization and public procedures
source.paraphrase: Public mutations are supported; publicProcedure.mutation is used in the official procedures guide. Authorization depends on the product.

invariants.why: Sign-up, contact, and other intentionally public writes exist. The builder name alone cannot establish an authorization defect.
invariants.fixHint: Build the mutation on protectedProcedure (or your authed procedure) so the caller is authenticated before the write runs.
invariants.avoid: This rule sees the builder chain only: publicProcedure followed by .mutation in one chain. It does not read the auth model, so a protectedProcedure that checks nothing is outside what the tree can see. Keep one procedure per chain statement.

source.work: tRPC documentation, input validation with zod
source.paraphrase: Input validators are needed when a procedure accepts input; no-input procedures are valid.

invariants.why: A procedure that accepts no input does not need an input validator, so missing .input alone is not a violation.
invariants.fixHint: Add .input(z.object({ ... })) before .query or .mutation describing exactly the fields the resolver reads.
invariants.avoid: The rule matches each builder chain on its own: a validated chain elsewhere in the file does not cover this one. .use(middleware) is not input validation. Keep one procedure per chain statement.

source.paraphrase: Output validation is optional; tRPC infers a mutation's result type from its resolver.

invariants.why: Requiring .output on every mutation is a policy choice, not a framework invariant.
invariants.fixHint: Add .output(schema) between .input and .mutation describing the value the mutation returns.
invariants.avoid: The validator must come before .mutation; .output placed after the mutation does not declare the contract. Queries are out of scope for this rule.

source.paraphrase: Query resolvers only read. Any create, update, delete, insert, upsert, or save belongs in a mutation, which the client caches differently.

invariants.why: Clients cache and refetch queries freely. A write hidden in a query runs again on every refetch and corrupts state.
invariants.fixHint: Move the write into a .mutation procedure and leave the .query to read the data the mutation changed.
invariants.avoid: The rule matches write method names (create, update, delete, insert, upsert, save) inside a .query chain kept on one line. A read helper with one of these names is a false positive; rename it.

source.paraphrase: createCaller should not be used to call procedures from within other procedures; extract the shared logic into a function and call it from each procedure.

invariants.why: A caller built inside a resolver creates context again and reruns every middleware and validator for work the outer procedure already authorized.
invariants.fixHint: Move the shared logic into a plain function that takes ctx (or ctx.db) and call it from both procedures.
invariants.avoid: router.createCaller(ctx), createCaller(ctx) from createCallerFactory, and createCallerFactory(router)(ctx) are the same call. Callers built outside a .query, .mutation or .subscription resolver, such as server components or scripts, are allowed.

source.paraphrase: TRPCError requires a predefined TRPC_ERROR_CODE_KEY string such as BAD_REQUEST, UNAUTHORIZED, FORBIDDEN, or NOT_FOUND rather than numeric HTTP statuses or custom strings.

invariants.why: Passing a numeric HTTP status (404) or an invented string ('UNAUTHENTICATED') falls back to INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR (500) and breaks client error handling.
invariants.fixHint: Replace the code with the matching official tRPC error code string (such as 'UNAUTHORIZED', 'FORBIDDEN', 'NOT_FOUND', or 'BAD_REQUEST').
invariants.avoid: Only literal string, template, or numeric values on the code property of new TRPCError({...}) are checked. Imported constants or variables are not resolved.

source.paraphrase: A tRPC middleware must return the result of calling next() (or await next(), inspect the result, and return it) so the procedure response and context reach the caller.

invariants.why: Calling next() as a bare statement discards the procedure's resolved output and returns undefined to the tRPC runtime.
invariants.fixHint: Return next({ ctx }) directly, or assign const result = await next({ ctx }) and return result afterwards.
invariants.avoid: Express middleware (which takes (req, res, next) and calls bare next()) should not be registered via t.middleware.
